Returns a visible label and its associated current page content; pages, blog posts and attachments are listed, with the type filter; page templates carry no labels.
The background page operations are listed, with the status and message each reports.
One task is read back, for both a successful and a failed operation, including the 404 for an unknown id.

Lists what a source is related to, filtered by the far entity type and by content status and version, expanding relationData, source and target, and directing favourite and like reads to their own endpoints.
Reads one relation, 404 when it does not exist, with relationData naming who created it and when.
Lists what is related to a target; relations are one way, so this answers a different question from the source listing rather than mirroring it.

CQL search across pages, blog posts, comments, attachments and spaces with 18 fields, AND/OR/NOT and brackets, IN and NOT IN, currentUser/currentSpace/favouriteSpaces and the relative date functions, ORDER BY, cqlcontext scoping, excerpt strategies and cursor paging; every branch carries the reader's own visibility rules, so results and totals exclude what they may not open.

Reading the look and feel is tested for the site and for one space, including the whole structure and the 404 for an unknown space.
The system information is tested, including the cloud id, site title and base URL; commitHash is empty.

The site's assigned theme is tested; a site with none reports none rather than the default. No pinned operation assigns one.
Reading one theme is tested, including the default by key and the 404 for an unknown one.

Reading the settings is tested; it needs only the permission to view the space.
The states a space suggests are tested, including the 404 for an unknown space; configuring them is not reachable through any pinned operation.
Lists pages in a content state with start/limit paging and v1 content expansions; body.export_view and body.styled_view expansions cap the page at 25.

Space administrators read whether content states are allowed and whether space-suggested and custom states are, with the suggested states listed only when allowed; administrators change the settings on the space page and state writes enforce them.
Reading the theme is tested, including that a space with none set reports no theme rather than a default one.

Setting a state is tested by id and by describing a new custom one, including that it publishes a version without changing the body, that re-using a name keeps one state, and the refused id-and-description, empty request, bad colour, long name, missing status and unknown id.

All four positions are tested by the order a reader then sees, not by the status code; an unknown position, a move relative to itself and a move beneath its own descendant are refused. A target in another space moves the page with its subtree and the folders, whiteboards, databases and Smart Links beneath it, needs delete permission in the source space and add permission in the destination, and refuses a space homepage or a title the destination already shows; replicas receive every moved page with its new space. The page view offers the same move. The target may be a folder, whiteboard, database or Smart Link as well as a page, siblings of every kind share one stored order, and a move out from under a page recomputes which page's restrictions the moved content answers to.

Creates a relation between a user, space or content pair; favourite runs from a user to a space or content, creating an existing relation is idempotent, and making one for another person requires site administration.

Choosing which settings a space shows is tested, including that the site itself cannot choose because its look is the global one, the refused unknown type, the refused theme selection on a space with no theme, and that it is administration.

Updating name, description, homepage, type and status is tested, including the refused homepage outside the space, the refused status and type, the 404 for an unknown space and that it is administration.
Changing the settings is tested, including the refused content mode and that it is administration.
Selecting a theme is tested, including the unknown theme key and that it is administration.
Updating is tested, including the required template id and that a blueprint owns its template so the API will not write it.
Replacing a property is tested, including the version bump, the mismatched key, and that a member cannot write another person's property while an administrator can.
Ends the caller's admin key, idempotently; afterwards restricted content is hidden from the administrator again.
Deletes the calling app's property, idempotently, under the write:app-data:confluence scope.

Permission-scoped attachment properties support JSON values, key filtering, cursor pagination, immutable optimistic versions, expansion, conflict handling and deletion. Every content kind Confluence gives properties — pages, blog posts, attachments, comments, custom content, folders, whiteboards, databases, Smart Links and spaces — has its own property routes here.

Blog metadata supports permission-filtered labels and label discovery, member likes, permission-shaped operations, optimistic versioned JSON properties, built-in classification set/reset, privacy-shaped synchronized actions, and an accessible author UI; v1 label writes act on blog posts, and the pinned v2 API has no label or like writes; classification uses the organization's levels with space-default inheritance; blog attachment, comment, custom-content and redaction routes are implemented.

Blog posts support public or creator-private current/draft creation, permission-filtered global and space collections, exact reads, optimistic updates, immutable version history/detail, trash, restore, purge, privacy-shaped actions and an accessible author UI; attachments, footer and inline comments, labels, likes, properties, classification and redaction share the page routes; drafts of published blog posts are saved at version 1 beside the published version, read with get-draft, discarded with draft=true and replaced by publishing; purge moves trashed posts to the deleted state that space administrators see and restore.
Deletes a comment property for a caller who may edit the comment.
Removing a property is tested.
Deleting is tested, including the refusal while a child is still there.

Database JSON properties support filtered cursor-paged reads, create, exact-id reads, optimistic version updates and deletion with database privacy, inherited visibility and atomic action records. Every change keeps an immutable version row; the pinned API publishes no property history read, so none is served.

Database containers support public or creator-private creation, current reads with optional expansions, inherited page/space permissions, nonempty deletion checks, privacy-shaped actions and a space UI journey. Columns, rows and saved views are edited on the database page; pages can sit beneath a database (not a private one), an archived database reads back, and moving (beside or beneath any node, to a space's top level or to another space), renaming, archiving with or without its contents and restoring are offered through the space's content tree, since Confluence publishes no REST operation for them.

Smart Link JSON properties support filtered cursor-paged reads, create, exact-id reads, optimistic version updates and deletion with inherited visibility and atomic action records. Every change keeps an immutable version row; the pinned API publishes no property history read, so none is served.

Smart Link creation, validated optional HTTP/HTTPS embed URLs, current reads with expansions, nonempty deletion checks, inherited page/space permissions, action privacy and the space UI journey are tested; pages can sit beneath a Smart Link, an archived one reads back, and moving (beside or beneath any node, to a space's top level or to another space), renaming, archiving with or without its contents and restoring are offered through the space's content tree, since Confluence publishes no REST operation for them; in the browser a Smart Link opens as a card with its destination, host and a sandboxed preview of HTTPS destinations.

Folder JSON properties support filtered and cursor-paged reads, create, exact-id reads, optimistic version updates, duplicate-key rejection, deletion, inherited visibility, and atomic action records. Every change keeps an immutable version row; the pinned API publishes no property history read, so none is served.

Folder creation, current reads with supported expansions, nonempty deletion checks, inherited page/space permissions, synchronized action privacy, and the nested-folder space journey are tested; pages and content of every kind can sit inside a folder, an archived folder reads back, a folder still holding a page cannot be deleted, and moving (beside or beneath any node, to a space's top level or to another space), renaming, archiving with or without its contents and restoring are offered through the space's content tree, since Confluence publishes no REST operation for them.
Deletes an author-owned page or attachment comment, or an administrator-moderated comment, with cascading replies and the documented 204 behavior.

Durable page inline-comment threads support exact storage-text anchors, replies, open/resolved/reopened state, optimistic versions, documented page/global/item/child collections, operations and like reads, cursor pagination, permission-filtered private sync actions, and an accessible author UI; blog posts take the same threads; bodies are written as storage, the document format or wiki markup and read in every primary format; anchors follow page and blog edits, versions and redactions, dangling when the passage is gone and reattaching when it returns; single reads take every include flag.

Moves a writable childless current page to trash through the canonical optimistic page command while preserving history and enforcing heterogeneous-child safety; an archived page can still be trashed; draft=true discards drafts and never-published pages, purge=true moves a trashed page to the deleted state with space administration, and deleted pages are visible to and restorable by space administrators.

Deletes an exact property from a writable current page atomically and emits a permission-filtered tombstone action; apps need the operation's Connect scope, enforced per operation from the pinned specification.
Site administrators delete a custom role and its assignments in every space, answered 202 with a finished long task; system roles cannot be deleted.
Space administrators clear a visible space's default; content without its own level then has no classification.
Workspace administrators delete an exact property from its space with an atomic delete sync action; apps need the operation's Connect scope, enforced per operation from the pinned specification.

Serves a scaled image thumbnail of a visible request attachment, or Jira's default file thumbnail for other files, as Jira's attachment thumbnails do.
